questions.q: What Azure subscription role do you need to create a Microsoft Purview account?
options: Contributor or Owner (or subscription Administrator)
Global Administrator in Microsoft Entra specifically
No role is required, anyone can create one
Reader
questions.explain: You need Contributor or Owner on the Azure subscription (or be an Administrator of it) to create a Microsoft Purview account.

questions.q: How many Microsoft Purview accounts can a tenant normally have under standard quota rules?
options: Zero — accounts must be created by Microsoft support
Exactly one
Unlimited
Exactly ten
questions.explain: Under normal quota rules, you can only create one Microsoft Purview account per tenant. If your organization already has one, the creation wizard won't let you make a second.

questions.q: Why does the location field on the Basics tab matter more than most other fields in the creation wizard?
options: It is automatically randomized regardless of what you select
It determines where your account's metadata is physically stored, and a Purview account cannot be moved to a different region after creation
It has no real consequence and can be changed anytime
It only affects the color scheme of the portal
questions.explain: The location is where your account's metadata is stored, and per this lesson, you cannot move a Purview account to a different region after creation — making it one of the hardest choices in the wizard to undo.

questions.q: What does the Purview environment tag (Production, Test, Dev, etc.) applied on the Tags tab actually do?
options: It's purely for the organization's own clarity and billing — Purview itself doesn't read or enforce it
It automatically deletes the account after 30 days if set to "Test"
It enforces different feature sets depending on the value
It changes the account's region
questions.explain: The environment tag is an organizational convention for your own clarity and billing grouping. Microsoft Purview itself does not read or enforce behavior based on this tag's value.

questions.q: What does Microsoft recommend to protect a production Purview account from accidental deletion?
options: An Azure Policy using the denyAction effect, blocking the delete action on Microsoft.Purview/accounts resources tagged Production
Disabling all user access to the account permanently
Nothing is needed — Purview accounts cannot be deleted
Changing the account's password weekly
questions.explain: Microsoft recommends creating an Azure Policy with the denyAction effect that matches Microsoft.Purview/accounts resources where tags.environment equals Production, blocking the delete action outright — ideally set up before real governed data lives in the account.
